si.how: Mentor lines from the Game Design Spec v2 (written with Claude, reviewed by the team); one line given a unit (minus 130 °C)

lines: Nobody passes their first sim. Not even me.
Welcome back, cadet. That was the hard part: starting.
First sims are for finding out what you don't know yet.
Textbook. Mission planners would frame that run.
You made those trade-offs look easy, and they aren't.
Plan ahead, then adapt. That's how real crews do it.
You made it, but {resource} was almost gone. Real missions keep a safety margin.
That emergency on turn {turn} was scary. What would you do differently?
A win is a win. Next time, finish with something to spare.
Everyone's safe, and that matters most. But the science didn't get done.
Safe AND useful, that's the real target.
Sometimes a mission needs a little risk to do its science.
The batteries ran dry on turn {turn}. Power only comes from the Sun, so saving it is the only way to have more later.
Every system wanted power at once. Which one could have waited?
{card} drained more than it looked.
Lunar nights last two weeks. Power you save by day is heat you'll need at night.
The cold won on turn {turn}. Would burying the habitat have helped?
At minus 130 °C, every bit of insulation counts.
Nobody's bringing groceries. The greenhouse is your lifeline.
Plants need time. Planting earlier would have helped.
{card} cost more food than it looked.
Your badge filled up, so the crew is going home early. That's a real rule: astronauts who reach their limit stop flying.
Shelters cost time, but they save your career.
The forecast warned you on turn {turn}. Were there cells left for the shelter?
